summary: FBRX 2.3.2 Beta (Weft): your own requests to this computer’s AI go ahead of help for the mesh, and FBRX Server becomes a file server.
notes: Your requests first: the AI on this computer answers one request at a time, and your own now start before help for other computers on FBRX Mesh (Mesh Assist, a lent model). Help that already started finishes first, and Mesh Assist shows who is waiting. Mesh Assist → This computer’s own requests go first turns it off.
FBRX Server 1.4.2 (below) adds a file server, FBRX Time backups seen coming online, and Ask the AI from anywhere in its console.

server.summary: FBRX Server 1.4.2: a file server with backups to a NAS, FBRX Time backups seen coming online, and Ask the AI from anywhere in the console.
notes: File server (the files role): share folders from the server itself, or make one of its virtual machines the file server. Accounts of their own, priority for its traffic, and backups to a NAS every night that keep changed and deleted files for as many days as you choose. On a gate, one button adds the firewall rule your networks need.

FBRX Time: a boot check gives the throwaway machine a private test network that reaches nothing else and sees it come online. When a check fails or warns, the server’s AI says what most likely went wrong.
Ask the AI: a button on virtual machines, the gate, the firewall, hardware, storage, roles and the terminal opens a chat with the server’s AI about what you are looking at.
The server’s own people go first on its AI, ahead of work for the mesh.
From 1.1: sudo fbrx-server update check, then sudo fbrx-server update commit; sudo fbrx-server roles add files adds the file server.

digger.summary: FBRX Digger 1.1.1: smaller and simpler, with device consoles in the Network Center and clearer sign-in errors.
notes: Links open in your own browser; Digger has no browser or edition settings of its own.
Device consoles (SSH, Telnet) are a tab of the Network Center; a sign-in that fails says why, and trying again keeps the device's key; a successful SSH sign-in opens its session.
Digger has its own tray icon and menu.
